name: Enemy Tier Scaling
description:
Keeps a wolf from being a joke at level five and a raid boss at level six. Given a player level or zone band it produces the multiplier set — health, damage, XP reward — that anything spawning enemies should apply. It deliberately owns only the curve, not the spawn: world.mob_patrol and world.dynamic_encounter_spawner decide when and where, and combat.damage_resolver never sees these multipliers, because scaling belongs at spawn time — applying it inside the damage pipeline would double-count it on every hit. Owning the curve in one place is what makes 'zone two feels too easy' a one-file fix instead of an archeology expedition. TWO READINGS OF ONE CURVE, and it only ever published the first. `multipliersFor` measures a GAP — how much stronger this enemy is than the player expects — so at parity it returns 1, which is correct and is not growth: a level-8 wolf matched to a level-8 player comes out identical to the level-1 wolf a level-1 player met, and a build that scales this way produces a world that never gets bigger while looking like it should. Found by playing to level 5 and measuring a multiplier of 0.76 on enemies that had never changed.

`statsAtLevel` is the other reading: the same curve measured from level 1, which is what a spawner needs to decide what a level-8 creature actually IS. The two are not redundant — one answers "is this fight fair" and the other answers "what am I making" — and keeping both here is what stops a spawner growing a second curve of its own, which would be the second place difficulty is decided.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: scalingCurve
inputs.description: linear | exponential | banded. Banded snaps enemies to fixed tiers per zone; linear and exponential interpolate. The curve is a content statement, not just math.

inputs.name: statsPerLevel
inputs.description: Fractional stat growth per level of gap. 0.08 keeps a ten-level gap meaningful without making it a wall; exponential curves should start lower.

inputs.name: maxLevelGap
inputs.description: Beyond this gap the curve clamps, so endgame players trivializing starter zones is a feature, and starter players wandering into the endgame get a firm no.

inputs.name: scaleRewards
inputs.description: Whether XP and loot tier scale alongside stats. Decoupling these is how you get degenerate farm spots; couple them until you have a reason not to.

outputs.name: currentMultiplierSet
outputs.description: health/damage/reward multipliers for the current context.

outputs.name: statsAtLevel
outputs.description: The multiplier set for a creature OF a given level, measured from level 1 rather than against the player — health, damage and xpReward for what a level-N version of something is worth. Asked at spawn by whatever decides a creature's stats, synchronously, for the same reason multipliersFor is a query: an event arrives a frame after the unit does.
